# 2.5D presentation techniques for WOLF//OVERRIDE on Godot 4.7 GL Compatibility

Read-only research. No files were edited. All doc citations are the official 4.7 pages fetched today; where a page is silent on Compatibility I say so instead of guessing.

## 1. What the project does today (baseline)

Source: `apps/game/scripts/main.gd`, `scenes/main.tscn`, `project.godot`.

- Renderer: `renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"` for desktop and mobile; viewport 960x540, `canvas_items` stretch; `textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true` but every PNG imports with `compress/mode=0` (Lossless) and `mipmaps/generate=false`, so no VRAM compression is actually in play.
- Scene graph is flat: `Main` (Node2D) draws the room painting itself in `_draw()` via `draw_texture_rect(CORRIDOR_BACKGROUND, Rect2(0, 60, 960, 540))` (main.gd:158-160); `records_room.gd:57-59` does the same for the records plate. The 1672x941 paintings are stretched to 960x540 and move 1:1 with the world, so there is no parallax, no lighting, no CanvasModulate, no shaders, no particles, and no Parallax2D anywhere.
- Layering already uses `z_index`: props 1, actors 2, intro gate 3, cage 4, WOLF pushed to 5 during the intro (main.tscn:112-171, main.gd:119-122, 293).
- One `Camera2D` (`IntroCamera`) does all the work: gameplay zoom `GAMEPLAY_ZOOM = 1.18`, X clamped manually to `[half_view, 960 - half_view]` at fixed Y 330 (`_update_gameplay_camera`, main.gd:165-167), `position_smoothing_speed = 4.0`; intro uses zoom 1.8 -> 1.95 and a tweened pan; chapter close tweens to zoom 1.25 (main.gd:870-875). Camera travel in gameplay is only about 960 - 960/1.18 = ~146 px, which caps how much parallax can ever show in these rooms.
- All UI lives on one `CanvasLayer` (default layer 1); the world canvas is below it. Status lights are `ColorRect`s, the relay spark is a `Line2D`.

## 2. Renderer facts that constrain every choice (verified)

From the renderers page (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/rendering/renderers.html), Compatibility column:
- "2D rendering features" - Yes. "MSAA 2D" - Not supported. "2D HDR Viewport" - Not supported. Compute shaders, particle trails, CompositorEffects, depth-of-field blur (3D), TAA/FXAA/SMAA, debanding - Not supported. Recommended when targeting "older mobile devices, or older desktop devices" and the only choice for web.
- Compositor page: "The compositor is currently a feature that is only supported by the Mobile and Forward+ renderers" and "Currently we only have access to the stages of the 3D rendering pipeline!" (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/rendering/compositor.html). So there is no engine post-processing stack for 2D on Compatibility; post effects must be CanvasItem shaders.
- Environment glow: "When using the Compatibility rendering method, glow uses a different implementation with some properties being unavailable... optimized to run on low-end devices" (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_environment.html), and 2D glow needs `use_hdr_2d` ("enables effects like 2D glow", https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_viewport.html) which Compatibility does not support. Fake glow must be additive sprites.
- 2D lights and shadows page (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/2d/2d_lights_and_shadows.html) contains no Compatibility restriction at all; 2D lights, shadows, CanvasModulate and CanvasTexture normal/specular maps are part of "2D rendering features". ProjectSettings exposes `rendering/2d/shadow_atlas/size` default 2048 and `rendering/2d/sdf/*` for all renderers (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_projectsettings.html). Note the `rendering/limits/opengl/max_renderable_lights = 32` / `max_lights_per_object = 8` settings describe positional 3D lights ("omnilights and spotlights"), not Light2D; the docs publish no 2D light cap for Compatibility, so keep counts small by design.
- GPUParticles2D runs on Compatibility except: "emit_particle() is only supported on the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility" and trails are unsupported (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_gpuparticles2d.html, renderers page). CPUParticles2D notes GPUParticles2D "may not run on older devices" (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_cpuparticles2d.html).
- Screen-reading shaders work in 2D on every renderer: "If a node uses hint_screen_texture, the entire screen is copied to the back buffer before drawing that node"; only `hint_normal_roughness_texture` is "Only supported in the Forward+ rendering method" (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/shaders/screen-reading_shaders.html). Blur via `textureLod` needs a `filter_*_mipmap` hint; the docs do not state whether Compatibility builds mipmaps for the 2D back buffer, so treat runtime screen blur as unverified on this renderer.
- Mobile cost model (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/performance/gpu_optimization.html): "Overdraw occurs when the same pixel on the screen is being rendered more than once"; "Transparency is particularly expensive where multiple transparent objects overlap"; "most Android devices do not support texture compression of textures with transparency (only opaque)". Import page (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_images.html): Lossless "is the default and most common compression mode for 2D assets"; VRAM Compressed "should be avoided for 2D as it exhibits noticeable artifacts"; mipmaps cost ~33% more memory; mobile/web "usually can't display textures larger than 4096x4096" (all current assets are below that).
- Texture memory today: each 1672x941 plate is ~6.0 MiB RGBA8 in VRAM uncompressed, each 2172x724 prop sheet ~6.0 MiB; three character sheets are drawn at scale 0.047-0.073 (so they are ~14-21x larger than displayed) with mipmaps off, which the import docs flag as the graininess case mipmaps exist to fix. Whole scene is roughly 30-50 MiB of texture: fine for phones, but every new full-screen plate adds ~6 MiB and one full-screen fill per frame.

## 3. Ranked techniques

Ranking weighs: effect on "reads as 3D", Compatibility support, mobile fill cost, and how much it fits the existing single-scene structure (rules: no scene-specific systems; presentation layers that apply to every room are fine).

### Do now

1. **Parallax2D plates (far / room / near)** - `Parallax2D.scroll_scale`, `scroll_offset`, `limit_begin/limit_end`, `follow_viewport` (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_parallax2d.html, tutorial https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/2d/2d_parallax.html: scroll_scale "values below 1 make layers appear distant (slower scrolling), while values above 1 make them appear closer"). ParallaxBackground/ParallaxLayer are "deprecated... Use the Parallax2D node instead" (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_parallaxbackground.html). Fit: move the two `draw_texture_rect` plates out of `_draw()` into `Parallax2D > Sprite2D` nodes (scroll_scale ~0.85-0.9) and add one near layer (scroll_scale ~1.15-1.25) with a dark pipe/cage silhouette strip and `z_index` above the actors. Because gameplay camera travel is only ~146 px, each plate shifts ~15-35 px; this is the honest ceiling unless rooms get wider or the camera gets look-ahead (item 3). Cost: one extra opaque full-screen fill per plate; keep to 3 plates on mobile. Art implication: the flat AI paintings must be split into at least a back plate and a foreground silhouette (two derived assets, each needing a manifest entry with source and rights). Zoom is always >= 1.18 here so the `repeat_times` zoom caveat does not apply; set `limit_begin/limit_end` so plates never show their edge at zoom 1.18.
2. **CanvasModulate + a few PointLight2D (no shadows) with Tween flicker** - "CanvasModulate is used to darken the scene by specifying a color that will act as the base 'ambient' color"; PointLight2D "shape is defined by a (usually grayscale) texture", "The texture's size determines the size of the light. The texture may have an alpha channel, which is useful when using Light2D's Mix blend mode" (2D lights page; https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_pointlight2d.html, https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_light2d.html). Fit: one CanvasModulate on the world canvas (UI is on its own CanvasLayer, and "CanvasLayers can be used to render things independently" per https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_canvasmodulate.html, so the HUD stays untinted), 3-5 lights per room: breaker/relay status lights (tie `energy`/`color` to the existing status ColorRects), WOLF's blue core in the intro, exit glow. Flicker: `create_tween().set_loops()` on `energy`; tweens default to `TWEEN_PAUSE_BOUND` so they stop with the pause menu (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_tween.html). Use a `GradientTexture2D` radial texture (built-in resource, no new asset). Cost: each light re-shades the pixels it covers for each lit CanvasItem; without normal maps `height` "only makes a visible difference on surfaces that use normal mapping", so skip it for now. Keep `shadow_enabled = false` in this pass.
3. **Camera2D: limits, look-ahead offset, tiny push-ins** - `offset` is for "looking around or camera shake animations"; `limit_*` plus `limit_smoothed`; `drag_*_margin`; `position_smoothing_*` already in use (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_camera2d.html). Fit: replace the manual clamp in `_update_gameplay_camera` with `limit_left/right`, add a 12-24 px look-ahead `offset` in the facing direction (tweened) and a 2-3% zoom push during station interactions. More camera travel directly amplifies item 1. Do not enable `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` (the Viewport docs say it fights "smoother movement, particularly with Camera2D smoothing"). Cost: none. Code-only; `tests/m0_scene_test.gd` may assert camera positions, so update with care.
4. **Full-screen vignette + colour tint overlay on the UI CanvasLayer, as the first child (under HUD)** - A `ColorRect` with a CanvasItem shader that outputs an alpha-blended or multiplicative vignette/grade needs no `hint_screen_texture`, therefore no back-buffer copy: one translucent full-screen quad, the cheapest possible cinematic framing. Custom post-processing page confirms the CanvasLayer + ColorRect approach and `SCREEN_UV` (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/tutorials/shaders/custom_postprocessing.html). Placing it as the first child of the existing `CanvasLayer` keeps the HUD, pause menu and title crisp above it (draw order within a layer follows tree order) and needs no new CanvasLayer. Film grain with `TIME` can live in the same shader. Cost: one full-screen transparent fill; acceptable on mobile.
5. **Asset pipeline hygiene for the existing AI art (no new generation)** - Downsample the three character sheets to roughly 2x display size (or enable `mipmaps/generate` on them: "prevent graininess when scaling down", +33% memory) so sprites stop shimmering; keep plates Lossless (import docs); keep everything under 4096 px; split the plates into layers for item 1. Each resized/derived file is a changed asset and needs its `assets/manifest.json` entry updated with source and rights. Cost: reduces VRAM and bandwidth.
6. **CPUParticles2D dust motes / sparks** - CPU particles run everywhere; a few dozen slow motes in the light cones and a short spark burst on the relay reads strongly as volume. GPUParticles2D also works on Compatibility except `emit_particle()` and trails, but for <100 particles CPU is simpler and behaves identically headless. Cost: negligible; use `CanvasItemMaterial` additive blend for sparks.

### Later

7. **Floor reflections by mirrored sprite** - A second `Sprite2D` per actor with `flip_v`, `scale.y` ~ -0.35 under the feet, `modulate.a` ~0.25 and a small CanvasItem shader (or `GradientTexture2D` mask via `clip_children` on CanvasItem) that fades alpha with UV.y. Pure sprite drawing, works on every renderer. "Later" only because `m0_actor.gd` draws the body with a custom `_draw()`/sprite offset and the floor in the paintings is matte; test on a still first. Avoid the screen-texture version (one back-buffer copy per frame for a subtle effect).
8. **LightOccluder2D hard shadows from cage/props** - `shadow_enabled`, `SHADOW_FILTER_NONE` "fastest to render", PCF5 "slower", PCF13 "slowest... should be used sparingly" (Light2D page); `occluder_light_mask`, `sdf_collision` (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_lightoccluder2d.html); atlas via `rendering/2d/shadow_atlas/size` (2048 default). Strong on the containment-cage intro (WOLF's blue light through bars). Hold until lights exist and the painted plates' baked shadows are checked for conflicts; cap at 1-2 shadow-casting lights, `NONE` or `PCF5` on mobile.
9. **Normal/specular maps on props via CanvasTexture** - "allows using normal maps and specular maps in any node that inherits from CanvasItem"; "Godot expects the normal map to use X+, Y+, and Z+"; `specular_shininess` for a "wet" look (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_canvastexture.html); generate with Laigter per the lights tutorial, then raise light `height`. Doubles texture memory per sheet and the AI paintings have baked lighting that will fight it; worth it only for the prop sheets (breaker/relay/checkpoint) and only after item 2 lands. Derived maps need manifest provenance.
10. **Screen-reading colour grade (LUT) via hint_screen_texture** - Works on Compatibility; costs one full-screen back-buffer copy plus a full-screen pass per frame. Use `BackBufferCopy` with `COPY_MODE_VIEWPORT` if two screen-reading nodes ever overlap ("the second one will not use the result of the first one", screen-reading page; https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_backbuffercopy.html). Prefer item 4's overlay until a grade is actually needed.
11. **CanvasLayer `follow_viewport_enabled` + `follow_viewport_scale`** - Doc-endorsed "pseudo-3D effects, with increasing scales for foreground layers and decreasing scales for background layers" (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_canvaslayer.html). Alternative to Parallax2D for whole-layer scaling; Parallax2D is simpler and keeps lights on one canvas (lights and CanvasModulate do not reach other canvases), so only use this if a layer must be outside the lit canvas.
12. **Depth-of-field on the near layer** - Pre-blur the foreground silhouette in the art tool (free at runtime, just another plate) rather than a runtime screen blur; Compatibility has no engine DoF and back-buffer mipmap blur is undocumented for it.

### Avoid for this project

13. **Environment glow / HDR 2D for bloom** - needs "2D HDR Viewport", unsupported on Compatibility; Compatibility's glow is a reduced 3D path. Use additive sprites: "Additive sprites are much faster to render, since they don't need to go through a separate rendering pipeline" (lights page).
14. **MSAA 2D for smoother Line2D/polygons** - "MSAA 2D: Not supported" on Compatibility; use `Line2D.antialiased`/textured lines instead for the relay spark.
15. **CompositorEffects / compute-based post** - Mobile/Forward+ and 3D only.
16. **Runtime screen-texture blur or reflections on mobile** - extra full-screen copies and overlapping transparency, the exact cost the GPU optimization page warns about, for subtle gains.
17. **`y_sort_enabled`** - correct tool for top-down depth ("higher Y position are rendered in front", https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_canvasitem.html) but a side-view corridor is already ordered by explicit `z_index`; adding Y-sort would reorder WOLF/human unpredictably.
18. **GPUParticles2D `emit_particle()` or trails** - unsupported on Compatibility; design effects without them.

## 4. Mobile budget to hold while doing the above

Base viewport 960x540 scales to native phone resolution with `canvas_items`, so every full-screen layer is a native-resolution fill. Suggested caps: 3 opaque parallax plates + 1 translucent overlay (item 4) + at most 1 screen-reading pass (item 10, if ever); 3-5 PointLight2D per room, 0-2 with shadows, no PCF13; particles under ~100 CPU particles; keep plates Lossless and under 4096 px; add mipmaps only to sheets drawn well below 50% scale. Measure on a device before claiming anything about frame rate: rendered stills prove appearance only.

## 5. Notes on evidence quality

- Pages that 404'd: `tutorials/performance/optimizing_for_mobile.html` (replaced by the GPU optimization page) and the old `contributing/.../internal_rendering_architecture.html` (found at `engine_details/architecture/internal_rendering_architecture.html`, which confirms "All rendering methods feature 2D batching" and that a 2D SDF for LightOccluder2D is generated on demand).
- Unverified from docs: whether Compatibility generates mipmaps for the 2D back buffer (needed for `textureLod` blur); any numeric cap on Light2D count on Compatibility. Both are flagged in the ranking rather than assumed.
- Nothing here has been played; all "effect" judgments are about what the techniques render, not about feel or readability.

# Research: depth in 2D side-scrollers and a dimensional UI spec for WOLF//OVERRIDE

Read-only pass. No files were edited. Everything below is grounded in the fetched sources listed at the end and in the current worktree (`apps/game/scenes/main.tscn`, `scripts/main.gd`, `scripts/game_settings.gd`, `assets/fonts/game_theme.tres`, `tests/ui_controls_test.gd`). Appearance judgements come from the baseline stills in `scratchpad/evidence/game-p3/`; no hands-on play happened, so nothing here claims feel or readability was validated.

## 0. Things found in the repo that shape the spec

- **Baseline in-world stills are not clean.** The JSON dumps show `paused: true` for 12-*, 20-*, 21-*, 22, 23, 30-*, 31-*, 32, 33 (the focus-loss auto-pause in `main.gd:597-601` fired during capture) and `title_open: true` for 34-37 and 50-records-entry. ## 1. How acclaimed 2D side-scrollers make flat art read as deep space

What the sources actually say (only claims the fetched pages support):

- **Ori and the Blind Forest** - Moon Studios and Airborn describe "a layered painterly look that has depth to it and doesn't look as flat as 2D games often do"; work started from black-and-white silhouette block-outs, then over 7,000 hand-painted graphics (90+ tree graphics with leaf/branch variants) were combined so "we can give each graphic different lighting, color, and movement sets". Ori is deliberately small on screen so "you can see further ahead, and have more time to react" and to convey insignificance in a huge world.
- **Hollow Knight** - Team Cherry's Unity case study: hand-drawn PNGs "layered in a 3D environment", lighting handled "with soft transparent shapes" rather than a lighting system, plus the particle system; the 80.lv Silksong piece confirms "the world ... is actually composed of multiple layers" producing the parallax effect.
- **Dead Cells** - Motion Twin (80.lv): pixel backgrounds converted to normal maps so "a torch on the left of a statue will light up the statue from the correct direction while respecting its base colours", which lets them re-light a biome without redrawing; "lots of particles, an emphasis on motion and special effects, a 3D lighting system, and lots of shaders"; art direction pillars are a saturated palette, Celtic architecture and alchemy, and Gwenaël Massé's deep dive argues saturated backgrounds and characters keep "the attention of the eye to any new element appearing on the screen".
- **INSIDE / Limbo** - Playdead's GDC session: "local shadowed volumetrics", lighting authored as separate diffuse, specular and bounce-light entities, analytic primitive-based ambient occlusion, screen-space reflections used "to establish a sense of depth", and dithering "to get rid of distracting artifacts" (colour banding) - all in service of minimal colour.
- **Trine 2** - Frozenbyte (PCGH interview): deferred renderer with "50 to 100 visible dynamic lights" per scene, plus depth of field, screen-space reflections, wrap light, bloom and colour correction; "our renderer allows artists to use many dynamic lights per frame".
- **Rayman Legends** - UbiArt lets artists work "without thinking about polygons or textures or sizes" (GDC Vault, Chris McEntee).
- **Little Nightmares** - fixed 2.5D side-on camera, with towering scale making the player "feel every bit as tiny as Six truly is" and a single warm key (the Zippo / yellow raincoat) cutting "through the gloom"; off-screen audio cues matter because the camera does not show everything (Unreal interview, fetch blocked; summary via search).
- **Katana ZERO** - neon lighting was used deliberately to "blend the artists' different styles"; VHS grain; Sin City / John Wick as references.
- **Signalis** - a "minimalist colour palette, modern effects and a dash of anime" over PS1-era graphics (DCP jury), dark grey/brown base with sharp red reserved for cutscenes.
- **Blasphemous** - interviews reached only cover influences (Goya, Murillo, Velázquez; Castlevania, Souls), not technique; not used for rules.

### Transferable rules for a 960x540 painterly military sci-fi corridor

1. **Five planes, not one painting.** Far (the existing painting, scroll 0.85), mid (machinery/props, 0.95), play plane (actors and stations, 1.0), near foreground (pipes, rails, grates cut from the props sheet, 1.2-1.3), and an atmosphere plane (fog/shafts) between far and mid. Hollow Knight and Silksong are literally "multiple layers"; Ori's depth comes from layered painted graphics. On single-screen rooms the parallax only shows during the intro camera moves (pan 300 to 576, zoom 1.95 to 1.25) and future follow-camera moves, which is fine: those are the moments where depth is noticed.
2. **Value structure by plane.** Highest contrast and saturation on the play plane and interactables (Dead Cells' saturation-draws-the-eye rule), lower contrast and cooler tint on far planes (atmospheric perspective: modulate the far layer towards `#0d1b2a`, about `Color(0.78, 0.86, 0.95)`), near silhouettes nearly black (`#050a12` at 0.85-0.95 alpha).
3. **Few lights, strong direction.** Author 2-4 light sources per room matching what the painting already shows (cold overhead lamp, cyan door light, amber breaker/relay) and make every added effect agree with them - the Dead Cells normal-map point is about light direction consistency; Hollow Knight shows soft additive shapes are enough. Keep real `PointLight2D`s under ~8 per room given the Compatibility cap.
4. **Light shafts and fog as the atmosphere plane.** Two or three elongated, skewed additive gradients at 8-15% alpha with a 6-10 s alpha drift (INSIDE's volumetrics in cheap form), plus a flat fog gradient at 15-25% over the far plane.
5. **Foreground silhouettes frame, never block.** Place dark, slightly blurred (lower-resolution region) cutouts at the screen edges and along the bottom; never over the actor path, stations, labels or the choice buttons. Ori's lesson: the player must see ahead.
6. **Particles sell air.** 30-60 slow dust motes (1-2 px, 4-10 px/s, 0.15-0.3 alpha, additive) across the whole room; a handful of warm embers near the breaker when armed. Dead Cells and Hollow Knight both lean on particle systems.
7. **Reflections anchor the floor.** A flipped, squashed, cyan-tinted copy of the actors at ~0.18 alpha fading downward reads as a wet deck and ties the sprites to the ground (INSIDE's SSR "to establish a sense of depth"; the title key art already paints a wet floor).
8. **Camera as a depth instrument.** Smooth follow with look-ahead and room limits, a small zoom-in (1.0 to 1.06-1.08, 0.5 s cubic ease-out) when dialogue or a choice opens, zoom-out to show the route; Ori's "small character, more reaction time" argues against a tight zoom during movement. Feel must be validated by play; this is the one rule that cannot be judged from stills.
9. **One cold base, one warm accent, red reserved.** Navy/teal world light with amber only for warnings and armed states, red only for alarm/story beats (Signalis' red; Returnal's teal from CRT and night-vision gear). Match UI cyan to the world's door/lamp cyan so the HUD looks lit by the same room.
10. **Grain hides banding.** Large soft gradients on 8-bit Compatibility output band; a 3-5% animated noise overlay (INSIDE's dithering, Alien: Isolation's VHS) hides it and adds film texture. Keep it under the UI layer.
11. **Vignette for lens depth.** A radial darkening (transparent centre to `#02060c` at 0.5-0.6 at the corners) between the world and the HUD.
12. **Regenerate AI art as layers, not paintings.** Ask the image tool for separate far wall / mid machinery / foreground pipes with alpha, a stated light rig (overhead cold lamp left, cyan door glow, amber panel), lower contrast in the far plane, a clean floor band for reflections, and 1920x1080-plus resolution so the 1080p stills stop softening (the current 1672x941 paintings are displayed at 0.574x at 960 and upscaled at 1080p). Every regenerated file keeps its provisional manifest entry with source, terms and rights status.

## 2. Dimensional, non-terminal menu and HUD design

What the references give:

- **Dead Space** - Dino Ignacio's goal was to "remove a wall of safety between the player and the game"; the remake keeps turquoise on interactables and "a glowing light" on everything of interest, but the UX case study warns that low-contrast blue holographic text with blur "made the texts blurry" - glow must not touch body text.
- **Returnal** - "gameplay first"; palette is "a haunting teal" from monochrome CRTs and night-vision gear; the UI is "chunky and clunky ... no gradients or elaborate transitions", "little to no directional motion, everything flickers on and off"; critical data sits near the focus point and peripheral content stays peripheral; colour-blind palettes and intensity sliders.
- **Destiny** - flat "Metro"-like layers brought alive by motion that "provides meaning": cursor slows over clickable targets, an "animated glimmer" marks updated items, cursor position moves "a number of parallax layers" but "overuse becomes fatiguing"; "the bigger the text, the more important", "colour equals expandability".
- **Alien: Isolation** - the 1979-set rule: nothing that could not have existed on the original set; the aesthetic lives in material (beige plastic, bevels, VHS softness) rather than in effects.
- **Control** - a "limited palette of utilitarian typefaces" (Basic Commercial, Interstate, ITC Avant Garde Gothic bold for area titles) makes the uncanny feel institutional; type does the atmosphere.
- **Hades** - menus are illustrated art plus After-Effects-built screen transitions and looping menu backgrounds rendered as PNG sequences; "hundreds of icons in a stylistically consistent way".
- **Mass Effect Legendary Edition** - unify the later games' UI improvements into the first without erasing its distinct feel (the lesson for Settings keeping its terminal identity).
- **Craft references** - NN/g: 100 ms for simple feedback, 200-300 ms for modals, enter slightly longer than exit, never 500 ms+, respect reduced-motion; NN/g glassmorphism: more blur is better over busy backgrounds, verify text contrast, give users a transparency control; Josh Comeau: one light source for every shadow, vertical offset about 2x horizontal, layered shadows, tinted (not black) shadows, lower opacity as blur grows; WebAIM: 4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text (18 pt / 14 pt bold) and 3:1 for component boundaries and focus indicators, no rounding.

Intro camera: zoom 1.8 -> 1.95, y=355, x 267 -> 300. Visible world window at gameplay zoom: 813.6 x 457.6 px, i.e. world y 101..559 of a background that spans y 60..600. Resolution headroom today: at a 1920x1080 window the gameplay view is 2.36 screen px per world px, so a 960-world-px background needs **~2266 px** of source width to be 1:1; the 1672 px paintings are upscaled ~1.36x in gameplay and ~2.2x during the 1.95 intro close-up. That is the concrete reason for "1920x1080 or larger" below (2560x1440 is the sensible target; 1920x1080 is only 0.85x of 1:1 at 1080p gameplay).

## 2. Maintenance corridor

**What already suggests depth**
- Three ceiling lamps at ~35%, 61%, 87% of the width (plus a small one at ~17%) paint cool light cones down the wall and leave vertical reflection streaks on the wet floor: the strongest depth cue in the image, and it already reads as a lit volume.
- The floor tiles converge toward a single vanishing point roughly at the centre of the wall/floor seam (one-point perspective, eye-level camera). A grate strip at ~73% of height and an under-deck of pipes below it make the walkway read as a raised platform with a pit in the foreground.
- Red emergency lamps on both ends (the lockdown mood), a large fan and a dense pipe ceiling with I-beams dividing the wall into bays every ~26% of width, atmospheric haze low-left and low-right.

**What blocks a parallax treatment**
- Single flat RGB raster: wall, lamps, floor and under-deck are one image. The floor must move 1:1 with the actors, so nothing in this image can move at a different rate without the seam tearing.
- Lamps are baked, so light cannot react to state (breaker armed, relay refusing) except by sprites drawn on top.
- The red lamp at x≈1320/1672 and the vent door at x≈1250 sit where the game draws the coolant relay (605) and the sealed door (780); the painting's own features and the live props overlap and compete at 960 px.

**Cheap tricks that apply with this art** (all built-in, all fine on GL Compatibility)
1. Floor reflections for actors and props: a second Sprite2D under each actor (`flip_v`, `scale.y ~ -0.55`, `modulate.a ~ 0.22`, z below the actor) with a canvas_item shader that multiplies alpha by `1.0 - UV.y`; the painting already has wet-floor streaks so reflected sprites look native. Should also be applied to the four station props.
2. Contact drop shadows: a soft ellipse (ImageMagick-generated 128x48 radial PNG, or `draw_circle` scaled) under feet at `modulate.a ~ 0.35`, tiny squash when moving. Grounds the inked characters on the painterly floor, which is the main style clash today.
3. Additive glow over painted lamps and prop lights: Sprite2D with `CanvasItemMaterial.blend_mode = BLEND_MODE_ADD` using a built-in `GradientTexture2D` (radial fill), placed at the three lamp x positions and over the breaker/relay/safe-point lamps; tint and alpha driven by the same state code that already sets `breaker_art.modulate`. This replaces the 18x5 `ColorRect` status lights visually. Note: the Compatibility renderer has no 2D glow post-process, so additive sprites are the only honest way to get bloom.
4. Slow fog/dust: one or two `Sprite2D`s with a `NoiseTexture2D` (FastNoiseLite, built-in, no asset) at `modulate.a ~ 0.08`, scrolled by `_process` or a uv offset; drawn above the background, below actors, with a top fade so it pools on the floor. Same for a second layer above actors at ~0.04 for foreground haze.
5. Foreground vignette: a `TextureRect` with a radial `GradientTexture2D` (transparent centre to `#02050a`) in the CanvasLayer under the HUD, alpha ~0.5. Cheapest "cinematic" cue; no asset needed.
6. Subtle camera parallax with the existing painting: draw it at `Rect2(-28.8 - (camera.x - 480.0) * 0.1, 56, 1017.6, 572.4)` (1.06x scale, 0.9x camera speed) and `queue_redraw()` from `_update_gameplay_camera`; or wrap it in a `Parallax2D` with `scroll_scale = Vector2(0.9, 1.0)`. Across the full 146 px camera travel the wall drifts ~15 px relative to the actors. Caveat: this moves the painted floor too, so actors appear to slide ~15 px on the floor over a full pan; it is subtle but it is a real artefact, which is why the layered regeneration is the proper fix.
7. Optional near layer from the same painting: a Sprite2D region of the under-deck strip (source rows ~690..941) drawn at `scroll_scale 1.08` over the base. The strip overdraws its own copy shifted at most ~12 px, which is invisible on a repetitive pipe pattern, and gives a cheap foreground cue without new art.

## 3. Records Access

**What already suggests depth**: same camera, same seam height (64%), same three-lamp rhythm (~20%, 61%, 87%) and the same under-deck, so the two rooms already cut together. Extra cues: server racks with rows of red LEDs recede in bays, railings in front of the racks, red lamps at both ends, haze low-left. The red LED rows are the best mid-layer candidate in either room.

**What blocks parallax**: identical to the corridor (one flat RGB raster). Additionally the live `_draw_exit()` and `_draw_machine_lights()` rectangles are flat colour rects on a painterly floor and look pasted on; they should become additive sprites in the same pass as the corridor lights.

**Cheap tricks**: all seven above apply unchanged; the reflection trick is even more effective here because the floor has stronger painted streaks. Red LED rows are a natural target for a slow additive flicker sprite (alpha noise, not a new system).

## 4. Title key art

Single flat painting with Rowan and WOLF baked in at the left, a distant gantry/bridge upper-left, the door mid-ground and crate silhouettes bottom. There is no camera on the title, so parallax here would be a slow time-based drift (±3 px, far layer only) or pointer-based. Fog, vignette and an additive pulse on the door lamp apply today. Proper layering needs an edit-mode pass that returns far (gantry, haze), mid (door wall), near (crates), plus the pair as a separate transparent cutout; the characters in the key art are the same designs as the sprites, so a cutout is consistent.

## 5. Characters and props (style notes for the regeneration)

- Rowan and the Director are hard-inked cel art with faceted shading; WOLF is painted-ink; the backgrounds are photoreal-painterly. The mismatch is tolerable at 72 px but it is what makes them look "stuck on". Drop shadow + reflection is the cheap fix; a future character pass should ask for softer, thinner line weight and painterly rendering so they match the environment.
- Rowan's sheet shows a baked red radial glow behind him (manifest says RGBA; the glow is not visible in the in-game captures, so it is in the transparent region, but worth a check before any re-export).
- Props are front-facing with a slight top-down view that matches the eye-level backgrounds; they have no cast shadows and no ground contact, which the shadow/reflection tricks fix. Resolution is fine: 543 px source -> ~120 world px -> ~280 screen px at 1080p.

## 6. Trial parallax set: `scratchpad/art/layers/`

Only **`corridor-far.png` exists (1920x1080, RGB, no alpha)**. `corridor-mid.png` and `corridor-near.png` **do not exist**, so the set cannot be judged or used as three Parallax2D layers yet.

Judgement of `corridor-far.png` against the current corridor:
- Consistent: eye-level one-point perspective, seam at the same 64% height, wall bays with I-beams, horizontal pipe runs, cool cyan lamp light, wet floor reflections. Mean colour srgb(6.8%, 12.2%, 15.1%) vs the current corridor's (7.3%, 10.7%, 12.7%): slightly brighter and bluer, within tint-correctable range (`modulate` or a one-off ImageMagick level match).
- Not a "far" layer: it contains the floor (which must scroll at 1.0) and the wall with lamps, so it is really a full base plate. If used as the far layer at 0.9x, the floor would slide under the actors.
- Lost content vs the current corridor: the fan, both red emergency lamps, the under-deck pipes and grate, railings, the vent door, the dense ceiling pipe run and most grime. It reads cleaner and more "clean concrete" than "grounded military sci-fi + dark painterly horror"; the red accent that carries the lockdown mood is gone.
- Lamp positions moved to ~14%, 50%, 86%. The breaker (x=350/960 = 36%) and relay (63%) currently sit inside lamp pools; with this plate they would sit in the dark between lamps, so either the lamps must stay at the original positions or the props move.
- Verdict: good as a **reference/base plate** for a cleaner regeneration, not a drop-in replacement. Generate mid and near with alpha from it, keep the lamp x positions of the original, and restore the red lamps and under-deck.

## 7. Prompt plan: layered regeneration with Codex image_gen (edit mode, existing paintings as references)

Common constraints for every prompt:
- "Side-view game backdrop, eye-level camera, strict one-point perspective, vanishing point at the exact horizontal centre on the wall/floor seam at 64% of the image height. No characters, no text, no UI, no lens distortion. Grounded military sci-fi research station, dark painterly horror, wet concrete and steel, cool cyan key light from ceiling fixtures, red emergency accents, heavy grime." Attach the existing room painting and `corridor-far.png` as references and say "match this palette, lamp colour and seam height exactly".
- Size: request the largest 16:9 the tool returns (today it returned 1920x1080); target **2560x1440** for far/mid/base; if the tool cannot exceed 1920x1080, upscale 2x with Lanczos in ImageMagick and record that step in `modifications`. Compose with ~6% safe bleed on the left and right so layers can be displayed at 1.06x and scrolled.
- Transparent layers: ask for "PNG with real alpha, nothing else in the frame, no drop shadow onto empty areas, no white fringe"; verify with `magick layer.png -alpha extract` that empty regions are fully transparent.
- Props: 1024x1024 per prop on transparency, same three-quarter-front angle as the existing sheets, with a soft baked contact shadow that does not extend past the base, lamp regions in a flat saturated colour so additive glow sprites can sit on top.

### Maintenance corridor — layer list
1. `corridor-far.png` (RGB, scroll 0.90): back wall only, the wall ending at the seam, lamps at 35%/61%/87% (plus the small one at 17%), light cones painted, red lamp left end, fan, vent door; the floor region filled with the plain dark floor tone (it will be covered by the floor layer).
2. `corridor-mid.png` (RGBA, scroll 0.95): the I-beams, the pipe runs, railings and the ceiling pipe mass that sit in front of the wall; nothing below the seam.
3. `corridor-floor.png` (RGB, scroll 1.00): the wet floor from the seam down to the grate, with the lamp reflection streaks at the far layer's lamp x positions, nothing above the seam. This is the layer actors stand on.
4. `corridor-near.png` (RGBA, scroll 1.08): the under-deck pipes and grate edge plus a low fog band; the top edge is the grate line.
5. `corridor-props-v2.png` or four individual PNGs: breaker, relay, seal door, safe point, matching the existing sheet designs (attach it as reference) at 1024 px per prop.

### Records Access — layer list
Same five roles with records content: far = rack wall with red LED rows and lamps at 20%/61%/87%, red lamps both ends; mid = railings, I-beams, pipe runs; floor = wet floor with reflections; near = under-deck; props = purge queue, mirror port, exit, matching the existing records sheet.

### Title — layer list
far = gantry, distant lights, haze (RGB); mid = the door wall and console (RGBA); near = crate silhouettes (RGBA); characters = Rowan and WOLF pair as a transparent cutout matching the current key-art pose. All at 2560x1440.

### Consistency checks before a layer enters the repo
- Seam at 64% ±1% of height in far/floor; vanishing point within 2% of centre; lamp x positions match the room table above (compare column brightness profiles with `magick -crop` + `-format %[mean]`).
- Composite far+mid+floor+near at zero offset and compare to the reference with `magick compare -metric SSIM`; accept only when the flattened set reads as the same room (target SSIM ≥ 0.6 against the old painting, higher against `corridor-far`).
- Composite again at -15 / 0 / +15 px far offset and 0 / ±12 px near offset and inspect the seam for gaps or doubled edges.
- Mean colour per channel within ±3 percentage points of the current room painting; red accent present in both rooms.
- Alpha check: `-alpha extract` shows no haze or fringe outside the intended silhouettes; no baked shadows on transparent ground.
- Render a 960x540 and 1920x1080 still with the capture script and confirm the JSON `paused` flag is false before judging it.

### Manifest / provenance per output
Keep the seven required `future_entry_fields` and add the layer fields:
- `asset_id`, `path` (e.g. `apps/game/assets/layers/corridor-far.png`)
- `source_or_tool`: "Codex built-in image_gen tool, edit mode, 2026-10-08" (plus ImageMagick steps if any)
- `source_reference`: path of the prompt text in the ignored art notes, plus `references_used`: array of the asset_ids attached as references (e.g. `["maintenance-corridor-background-provisional", "corridor-far-trial-2026-10-08"]`)
- `generated_on`: "2026-10-08"
- `terms_reference`: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/
- `rights_review_status`: "Provisional AI-assisted environment layer, human reviewed. Final commercial asset-rights review remains open; not covered by the code/docs GPL license."
- `modifications`: exact size returned, any upscale (method and factor), alpha cleanup, crops; otherwise "no pixel edits"
- `layer_role` (far/mid/floor/near/prop) and `layer_scroll_scale` (0.90/0.95/1.00/1.08)
- `replaces`: the asset_id it supersedes, and `implementation_status`: which node draws it and in which rooms.
Update the top-level `status` sentence when the set lands and keep `merge_warning` intact.

## 8. Suggested order for the implementation pass
1. Vignette + fog + drop shadows + reflections + additive lamp/prop glows: no new art, apply to both rooms through the same small helper so it is a presentation layer, not a per-scene dressing. Rendered stills are evidence of appearance only; no feel claims.
2. Camera parallax on the existing painting at 0.9x/1.06x (accept the ~15 px floor slide for now) or the under-deck strip at 1.08x.
3. Regenerate the layered sets per section 7; swap to `Parallax2D` nodes with the scroll scales above and remove the slide.
